citations.M1: split it into a separate release a week later, after 0142 plus the backfill have soaked
citations.M2: Consider an intermediate app release that writes both `status` and `state` and reads `status` — it removes the whole ordering hazard in 7, 8 and 9
citations.M3: `Order.from_row` calls `OrderState(row["state"])` and every one of the 61M rows still has `state = NULL` until the backfill finishes, so `get_order` raises
citations.M4: The `CASE` has no branch for `PAID` (5,210), `canceled` (1,988), `complete` (417) or NULL (149), so 7,764 rows get `state = NULL` and 0143's `SET NOT NULL` fails
citations.M5: it pages with `OFFSET` while the `WHERE state IS NULL` set shrinks under it, so every second batch is stepped over
citations.M6: The whole backfill runs inside one `conn.transaction()`, so on 61M rows it is a single hours-long transaction holding a snapshot open
citations.M7: Dropping `status` breaks `jobs/nightly_finance_export.py`, which selects `o.status` and filters `o.status IN ('paid','shipped')` — the grep was scoped to `app/`
citations.M8: Before 0143, require `SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE state IS NULL` to return 0, as a gate rather than an assumption.
citations.M9: that's why staging reported 2,104,377 to do and "done: 1055000"
citations.M10: the downgrade recreates `status` empty, so once it runs there is no way back
citations.M11: ~1,600 rows/s (1.055M in 660s), so 61,437,902 rows is roughly 10 hours, not 11 minutes
citations.M12: `ALTER TABLE ... SET NOT NULL` takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and full-scans 61M rows
